title: Throat
intro: Throat asks whether an audience can hear a performance while failing to hear the person making it. The demands are basic: water, responsiveness, relief from pain. Language difference then turns literal incomprehension into a wider failure of care. Its repetitive complaint uses the injured instrument to report the injury, so the song itself cannot fully separate expression from further labour. The imagery intensifies because each explanation seems to fail. This is a close account of a humiliating stage experience, without enough evidence to identify a particular show.
reading: Attention is not care; the voice must continue working to communicate the cost of using it.

revisions.editorial-22-hurt-hook: The hook contains almost no figurative language. Before looking for a cultural code, take the complaint at its stated scale: the organ required to continue the show hurts. Repeating it makes the problem inseparable from the labour of reporting it. Each further vocal phrase is also another use of that throat. The song turns a condition usually hidden behind entertainment into the entertainment's unavoidable subject.
revisions.editorial-22-water: A mouthful of water is a small, immediately answerable need. Its absence makes the later fury legible without requiring the audience to accept every insult as a fair description of other people. He is publicly visible but privately unsupported. The contrast is not fame versus obscurity; it is being watched versus having somebody notice what would help.
revisions.22-understand: The first statement concerns people not understanding Chinese. Later, the language specification disappears and 'nobody understands' follows descriptions of blades and bloody phlegm. The song moves from translation to recognition: even without knowing every word, someone might register distress and respond. This is a useful limit for a listening-notes site too. Explaining the vocabulary answers one barrier in the lyric, while the lyric insists that understanding must amount to more than decoding.
revisions.editorial-22-blades: The sharp-object comparison tries to make an internal sensation available to somebody outside the body; blood then supplies a visible sign. Each attempt is followed by the same failure of understanding. The escalation is communicative as well as graphic: if a plain statement is not enough, perhaps this image will be. The return to the stage complaint at the end leaves the practical situation unchanged.
